title: throughput-regression-continuous-batching-debug-scratchpad-7
content:
Context:
- Regression noticed after 2024-11-05 rolling deploy (canary -> prod). Throughput for 4k token mixed-length workload dropped ~20-35% across Dedicated pools running model-rw-v1-7b-quant.
- Appears correlated with continuous-batching changes from feature branch continuous-batching-tuning (PR GH-PR#4821) that changed two defaults: batch_timeout_ms from 8 -> 12 and enable_prefix_cache_on_miss = true.
- Affected stacks: dedicated-gpu-pool-2 (A100s), dedicated-gpu-pool-3 (A10G). Hosted unaffected.

Observed impact (from last 72h dashboards):
- p95 latency increase from 190ms -> 260ms on token-level microbenchmark for batch sizes ~16
- Tokens/sec per-GPU down by ~22% on mixed-length synthetic workload (seq len 512/1024 mix)
- Error rates unchanged; KV cache hit-rate slightly higher (up ~3%)

Relevant config snippets (from rollout config):
- continuous_batching: { "batch_timeout_ms": "12", "max_batch_size": "64", "enable_prefix_cache_on_miss": "true", "autobatch_strategy": "adaptive" }
- runtime flags: --grpc-worker-count=8, --kv-cache-ttl-ms=60000

Quick logs and CLI checks I ran (timestamps local):
- curl metrics endpoint for a single worker:
  curl -s http://10.2.14.6:9090/metrics | grep batch | head
  => batch_queue_depth{pool="dedicated-gpu-pool-2"} 12
  => batch_dispatch_latency_ms_bucket{le="50"} 1234
  => batch_dispatch_latency_ms_bucket{le="200"} 4567

- Observed long tail in batch_dispatch_latency_ms distribution after 11/05 deploy.

Commands tried (experiments):
1) Rollback batch_timeout_ms to 8 on a small canary pool (dedicated-gpu-pool-2-canary):
   - applied config, restarted runtime on 2 nodes
   - Result: tokens/sec recovered ~12% (not full), p95 dropped ~30ms
2) Disabled enable_prefix_cache_on_miss on same canary:
   - Result: additional ~6% improvement; combined rollback -> near baseline (~95% of pre-regression throughput)
3) Increased grpc-worker-count to 12 (on canary) to see if worker saturation is the issue:
   - Result: negligible change, CPU not bottleneck, GPU utilization slightly higher but not saturated
4) Forced small batch_timeout_ms=4 (local dev only) to observe batching behavior:
   - Result: reduced dispatch latency but batching efficiency dropped (fewer tokens per batch) -> net throughput drop for mixed-length workloads

Log snippets (interesting lines):
- "WARN rpc_dispatcher.go:210 slow dispatch detected: wait_ms=19 batch_size=2 pool=dedicated-gpu-pool-2"
- "INFO kv_cache.go:88 cache_miss_prefix=true key=..." (many of these after 11/05)
- "DEBUG batching.go:147 merged_batch_count=3 merge_delay_ms=11"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Interplay between increased batch_timeout_ms and enable_prefix_cache_on_miss causes more frequent small-batch merge delays: when prefix-cache misses occur we delay dispatch to attempt cache warmup, but with timeout increased we are waiting longer leading to higher latency and suboptimal batching patterns. Explains higher KV hit-rate (more cache warmup attempts) and higher dispatch latency.
2) Kernel selection / compilation path regressions for certain sequence-length distributions: a config change in PR touched a path that selects slower kernels for mid-range seq lengths (512). Less likely because rollback of batching flags improved throughput.
3) Resource-level contention caused by new background compaction/eviction task that coincided with rollout (seen as small spike in io/writes on node); possible but no clear evidence in node-level metrics.

Notes on data and how I measured:
- Microbenchmark: local loadgen script (loadgen/mixed_seq.sh) sending 600 concurrent requests across 8 clients, target qps ~1800, run for 10m, record tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency.
- Metrics source: per-worker Prometheus metrics (batch_dispatch_latency_ms histogram, batch_size_avg, kv_cache_hit_rate), and per-GPU telemetry (utilization, SM%).

Experiments to validate hypotheses (done and planned):
- Done: rollback batch_timeout_ms -> partial recovery. Disabled prefix_on_miss -> additional recovery. So likely hypothesis 1 primary.
- Planned: run an AB experiment with three variants: (A) original defaults (timeout=8, prefix_off), (B) timeout=12 + prefix_off, (C) timeout=12 + prefix_on. Compare tokens/sec and p95 over 2h windows. Use canary pool tag and autoscaling off.
- Planned: add additional tracing around batch merging to capture per-request wait times and reason-codes (e.g., wait_for_cache_warmup vs wait_for_batch_full). If we already log reason codes, dump them to file for a 30-minute run.

Immediate remediation (what I did):
- Rolled canary back to batch_timeout_ms=8 globally for all Dedicated pools (manual emergency config) to stop customer impact. Sent alert to SRE/Triage.
- Opened GH-PR#5042 to revert continuous-batching-tuning defaults until we can safely reintroduce with tests.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need to confirm whether "enable_prefix_cache_on_miss" was intended to be default-on. If so, we need rigorous perf tests for mixed-length workloads.
- Verify if any other rollout touched background eviction tasks (check release-engineering changelog).
- Add synthetic test to CI that runs mixed-length batching perf for at least 20m at ~1k qps (so we catch regressions early).
- Decide on observability: add metric batch_wait_reason{reason="cache_warmup"} to make future triage easier.

Slack/threads and useful links:
- Slack: #serving-runtime thread "regression: throughput after batching change" (link pinned in PR comments)
- GH-PR#4821 (continuous-batching-tuning) -- contains config diffs and perf notes
- GH-PR#5042 (revert defaults emergency)
- JIRA: SERVE-917 incident ticket (timeline + pagerduty notes)

Notes-to-self (quick):
- When running AB tests, block autoscaler to avoid confounding factors.
- Capture full per-request trace for 1k requests (sampling=100%) for 15m.
- Talk to Miguel about adding instrumentation in batching.go to surface merge reason codes.

Bottom line: temporary rollback fixed most of the regression; root cause likely interaction between longer batch timeout + cache-warmup behavior causing delayed dispatch and smaller effective batch sizes for mixed-length workloads. Need to add tests and metric instrumentation before re-enabling new defaults.
